Shallow network: θ builds each unit, ϕ mixes them

Click any hi circle (or one of its arrows) to trace a single hidden unit through the network. Hover any arrow to see what its weight does. hi = a[ θi0 + θi1·x ]
y = ϕ0 + ϕ1h1 + … + ϕDhD
parameters = 3D + 1

plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels (a and b), each showing a diagram of a shallow neural network with one input node x, three hidden units h_1, h_2, h_3, and one output node y. In panel (b), two bias nodes labeled 1 are present — one feeding the hidden layer and one feeding the output — and the connections from hidden units to the output are labeled with weights φ_1, φ_2, φ_3 plus a bias weight φ_0; a single representative input-to-hidden weight θ_{11} is also labeled to indicate the notation convention. In panel (a), the weight labeling emphasizes the hidden-layer side: the bias connections to each hidden unit carry weights θ_{10}, θ_{20}, θ_{30}, and the connections from input x carry weights θ_{21} and θ_{31}, making the full first-layer parameterization explicit. Arrows in both panels use black and orange coloring to distinguish the input-side (pre-activation) connections from the output-side (post-activation) connections. This figure introduces the standard parameterization of a shallow network, showing how θ weights govern the input-to-hidden linear transformation and φ weights govern the hidden-to-output linear combination.

interactionPlan.concept: A shallow neural network is a single input fed through D hidden units — each hidden unit applies its own weighted-plus-bias linear function (θ) before a ReLU, and the output is a weighted-plus-bias combination (φ) of those hidden activations.
elements: Panel label 'a)' on the left half and 'b)' on the right half
Panel a: input node circle labeled x (black outline, left)
Panel a: three hidden node circles labeled h_1, h_2, h_3 (black outline, middle column, vertically stacked)
Panel a: small teal ReLU 'kink' glyph drawn inside each hidden node circle
Panel a: output node circle labeled y (black outline, right)
Panel a: orange bias node circle labeled 1 feeding the hidden layer (upper-left, orange outline and orange text)
Panel a: orange bias node circle labeled 1 feeding the output (top-center, orange outline)
Panel a: black arrows x -> h_1, x -> h_2, x -> h_3 (input-to-hidden connections)
Panel a: orange arrows bias1 -> h_1, bias1 -> h_2, bias1 -> h_3
Panel a: orange arrow output-bias -> y
Panel a: black arrows h_1 -> y, h_2 -> y, h_3 -> y (hidden-to-output connections)
Panel a: orange weight labels θ_10, θ_20, θ_30 on the bias-to-hidden arrows
Panel a: grey weight labels θ_11, θ_21, θ_31 on the x-to-hidden arrows
Panel a: orange weight label φ_0 on the output-bias arrow
Panel a: grey weight labels φ_1, φ_2, φ_3 on the hidden-to-output arrows
Panel b: identical node layout (x, h_1, h_2, h_3, y) with all-black arrows, no bias nodes, no weight labels
Arrowheads converging at y drawn as multiple overlapping black arrowheads
Optional equation annotation beneath panel a: h_i = a[θ_i0 + θ_i1 x], y = φ_0 + Σ φ_i h_i

interactions.label: Diagram view
interactions.teaches: The same network topology carries hidden parameters: the bare arrow diagram and the θ/φ-annotated diagram describe identical computation, one just names every parameter.
Each hidden unit owns exactly one slope θ_i1, one bias θ_i0, and one output weight φ_i — clicking traces that single unit's private path from x through the ReLU to y.

interactions.label: Number of hidden units D
interactions.teaches: The network's capacity is set by D: adding a hidden unit adds two θ parameters and one φ parameter, while x and y stay single nodes.

demo_steps.title: The bare network
demo_steps.narration: One input x fans out to three hidden units, which all feed a single output y. This is the entire architecture of a shallow network — no parameters shown yet.

demo_steps.title: Name every parameter
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the labeled view adds the two orange bias nodes and every weight name: θ_i0 and θ_i1 on the input side, φ_0 and φ_i on the output side.

demo_steps.title: Follow one hidden unit
demo_steps.narration: Click h_2: its incoming pair θ_20 (bias) and θ_21 (slope from x) form the pre-activation, the teal kink applies the ReLU, and φ_2 scales its contribution to y.

demo_steps.title: Grow the hidden layer
demo_steps.narration: Drag D up to six. Each new unit brings its own θ_i0, θ_i1 and φ_i, so the parameter count grows as 3D + 1 while the input and output remain single nodes.

demo_steps.title: Shrink to one unit
demo_steps.narration: With D = 1 the network collapses to a single kinked line: y = φ_0 + φ_1·a[θ_10 + θ_11 x]. Everything richer is just a sum of more such pieces.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A shallow network is nothing more than D independent copies of 'scale-and-shift x, clip it, then scale again' — the θ's build each hidden unit's kinked line and the φ's decide how much of each line to add into the output.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two side-by-side panels sharing an identical left-to-right node layout: input circle x on the left, a vertical column of hidden circles h_1..h_D in the middle, output circle y on the right, all white with black outlines and italic serif labels. Panel b (right) is the clean version: plain black arrows only, arrowheads piling up at y. Panel a (left) adds two salmon/orange bias circles labeled '1' — one up-left feeding every hidden unit, one at top-center feeding y — drawn in orange outline with orange arrows, while x-to-hidden and hidden-to-output arrows stay black. Weight labels sit just above each arrow: orange labels for bias weights (θ_10, θ_20, θ_30, φ_0), grey labels for signal weights (θ_11, θ_21, θ_31, φ_1, φ_2, φ_3). Inside each hidden circle draw a small teal ReLU kink glyph (flat segment joining a rising segment). When a hidden unit is clicked, bolden and saturate its three connected arrows and their labels while fading all other edges to light grey. The hidden-unit slider should re-space the column symmetrically about the x–y axis and renumber labels; bias arrows must re-fan to the new unit positions. Generous white background, no axes, no legend.

discrepancies: Label legibility: the SVG viewBox (1245×380) is scaled down into the available width, so the parameter names (θ11, θ20, ϕ1 …) render at roughly 5–6 px on screen and are effectively unreadable at inline size, whereas in the source they are clearly readable annotations.

The teal ReLU 'kink' polyline is drawn small and centred on the hidden circle so it overlaps/strikes through the h1/h2/h3 glyphs; in the source the teal kink is a larger stroke placed to the left of the label and reads as a separate, prominent element.

The θ11 / θ21 / θ31 labels are bunched very close together just right of the x node (and near the orange θi0 labels), producing a crowded cluster; the source spaces them out further along each edge with clear separation between grey and orange labels.
The figure sits in a tall container with a large band of empty white space beneath it, so the drawing occupies only the upper-middle portion — the source is a tight, wide two-panel strip.
Arrow/stroke weights and node outlines are proportionally thinner than the source's heavy black outlines and chunky arrowheads, giving a lighter, less emphatic look than the original.
evaluation.notes: Topology, two-panel composition, orange bias nodes/edges, grey weight labels and teal ReLU kinks are all faithfully reproduced with a rich, genuinely pedagogical set of interactions (step player, D slider, labeled-view toggle, click-to-trace), but the whole drawing is scaled down so far that the parameter labels are nearly illegible and the teal kinks collide with the h-subscript labels.
action_items: Shrink the viewBox (or increase base font sizes to ~18–22 user units) so θ/ϕ labels render at a comfortable ≥11 px on screen, and tighten the viewBox height so the panels fill the container instead of leaving a large empty band below.
Enlarge the teal kink polyline and shift it left of the node glyph (as in the source) so it no longer overlaps the h1/h2/h3 text; also nudge the h label so kink and label are clearly separated.
Increase separation along the x→hi edges for the θi1 labels and offset them further from the orange θi0 labels to remove the crowded cluster near the input node.
Thicken node outlines, edge strokes and arrowheads to better match the heavy black line weight of the source figure.

feedback.rationale: Concept, topology, and interaction structure are all correct; the issues are purely implementation-level (viewBox scaling, font sizes, label spacing, kink placement, stroke weights), so the generator should refine rendering.

discrepancies: Panel layout differs: the source places a) and b) side by side, while the generated figure stacks them vertically (the 'side' mode only triggers at aspect ≥ 2.6, which the default container does not reach), changing the overall composition at a glance.
The teal ReLU 'kink' inside each hidden unit is much smaller and thinner than in the source, where it is a bold teal polyline that spans most of the h circle and clearly reads as a clipped line.

Weight labels are rendered smaller than in the source and the subscripts are set very small (e.g. 'ϕ0' reads as 'ϕo', 'θ10' subscript nearly illegible at inline size); in the source the θ/ϕ labels are large and clearly readable.

Labels crowd the arrows more than in the source: θ11/θ20 and θ21/θ30 sit close together over the fan-out region, and the h-node labels are pushed right of centre inside the circles to make room for the kink.
evaluation.notes: Topology, arrowheads, bias nodes, orange/grey/teal colour scheme and all parameter names are faithfully reproduced with a rich, conceptually apt set of interactions (step player, labeled/clean toggle, D slider, click-to-trace), but the default vertical stacking instead of the source's side-by-side panels and undersized weight labels/teal kinks weaken the drop-in resemblance.

feedback.rationale: The concept, topology, and interaction design are faithful; the remaining issues are implementation details (side-by-side layout threshold, label/subscript sizing, teal kink scale, label crowding) that the generator can fix directly.

Click any hi circle (or one of its arrows) to trace a single hidden unit through the network. Hover any arrow to see what its weight does. hi = a[ θi0 + θi1·x ]
y = ϕ0 + ϕ1h1 + … + ϕDhD
parameters = 3D + 1
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: In panel a the weight labels are badly bunched: θ11, θ20, θ21, θ30 pile up just right of the x node and overlap each other and the bias arrows, whereas the source spaces them cleanly along each edge (θ11/θ21/θ31 below the black arrows, θ10/θ20/θ30 above the orange ones).
The θ31 label appears to be missing/hidden in the rendered panel a (only five of the six input-side labels are legible), so one input weight is effectively unlabeled.

Overall drawing scale is very small relative to the canvas — the two panels occupy a thin horizontal band with large empty margins above and below, making node letters (x, h1..h3, y) and all parameter labels uncomfortably small compared with the source's large, high-contrast typography.

The teal ReLU kink inside each hidden unit is rendered as a tiny tick barely visible at the default scale; in the source it is a bold teal bent line spanning most of the circle and is a key visual cue.

Arrowheads at y are thinner/less emphatic than the source's heavy converging arrowheads, and the orange bias node stroke/label weight is lighter, so panel a reads as faint rather than the source's strong orange accents.
evaluation.notes: Topology, two-panel composition and color scheme match the source and the interaction set (step player, D slider, label toggle, click-to-trace, tooltips) is rich and pedagogically apt, but the drawing renders far too small and the panel-a parameter labels collide in a cluster near the input node, badly hurting legibility and faithfulness.

feedback.rationale: Concept, topology, and interaction design are correct; the problems are implementation-level (label placement collisions, missing θ31 label, undersized drawing scale, faint ReLU kink and arrowheads) and should be fixed in the rendering.
